name: Ahmedabad–Dandi Highway

timeline.event: Mahatma Gandhi walks from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi along this route, 12 March to 5 April, and breaks the salt law on 6 April
Renumbered as NH 64; it had been NH 228, the Dandi Heritage Route
The National Salt Satyagraha Memorial opens at Dandi, at the highway's southern end

history: NH 64 joins the big city of Ahmedabad to the seaside village of Dandi, where Mahatma Gandhi's Salt March ended in 1930. From Ahmedabad it runs south as the Dandi Heritage Route, roughly following the path of the march through Kheda, Anand, Bharuch, Surat and Navsari to the sea, crossing the Mahi river on the way. Gandhi and a small group of followers covered that path on foot in 24 days, stopping each night in a village along the way. The route was made a national highway so the path could be protected and marked, and many of the halt villages now carry memorials. Along its length the road also passes some of India's busiest industry — the chemical estates of Ankleshwar and the diamond and textile mills of Surat.
facts: It retraces Mahatma Gandhi's famous 1930 Salt March from the Ahmedabad area to Dandi.
Ends at Dandi beach, where Gandhi broke the salt law on 6 April 1930.
Crosses the Narmada river at Bharuch, near the historic Golden Bridge.
About 386 km long, entirely within Gujarat.
Gandhi's marchers walked roughly 385 km of this route in 24 days, halting overnight in villages along the way.
Passes through Anand, the town where Amul and India's milk co-operative movement began.
significance: NH 64 is unusual among national highways because it is as much a memorial as a road — it preserves and signposts one of the most important journeys of India's freedom movement. It is also a working highway that threads through Gujarat's industrial heartland, linking Ahmedabad to the chemical, textile and port towns of the south, from Bharuch to Surat.

engineering.name: Narmada crossing at Bharuch
engineering.note: the river is more than a kilometre wide here; the 19th-century Golden Bridge of 1881, about 1.4 km long, still stands beside the newer crossings

engineering.name: Mahi river crossing
engineering.note: the road bridges the wide, tidal lower Mahi on the boundary between Anand and Vadodara districts

travelNotes: The whole road makes a popular one- or two-day heritage drive, with signboards and small memorials at the villages where Gandhi halted; the National Salt Satyagraha Memorial at Dandi is the natural place to finish. Traffic is heaviest around Ahmedabad and Surat, and the Bharuch–Ankleshwar stretch is busy with tanker and container trucks. Gujarat's roads here are good and food stops are frequent. Winter, from November to February, is the pleasant season; May and June are very hot.
